Encore 0.6.2: lighter on the CPU while music plays, especially on Linux.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.6.2_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.6.2_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ | `Encore_0.6.2_amd64.deb` |
| Other Linux (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore_0.6.2_amd64.AppImage` |

Encore 0.5 and 0.6 update themselves to this version: they download it in
the background and install it the next time you quit, or right away with
**Restart to update**. Updating keeps your session, settings and downloads.
From 0.4 or earlier, download it from this page.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** a fresh download asks you to choose **Open Anyway** in **System
  Settings → Privacy & Security** once. After an update, macOS asks once
  again for access to your saved session in the Keychain; choose **Always
  Allow**.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.

## Fixes

- **Less CPU while playing.** Encore redrew the seek bar, the lyrics and the
  playing bars on every frame of the screen. It now updates them ten times a
  second, which looks the same and costs about half as much. On Linux, where
  the AppImage draws on the CPU, the playing bars now stand still and the
  blurred cover behind the side panel's lyrics is a plain tint of its colour.
- **Less memory on Linux.** After finding a song's audio, Encore now gives
  the memory it used back to the system, instead of keeping a few hundred
  MB until it quits.

Encore is unofficial and not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
